title: Rome: major doctrines are only probable from Scripture until tradition locks the sense
source_text: XLVI. Sed contra istud urgent adversarii, non pauca esse quae sunt ad fidem magni momenti, quae ex Scriptura quidem aliquo modo deducuntur; Sed non ita certo atque evidenter, ut in eo possit animus firmiter acquiescere, ac dubium omne tollatur, donec adhibeatur traditionis authoritas, quae verum Scripturae sacrae sensum confirmet, & extra dubium ponat. Atque in exemplum afferunt doctrinam de aequalitate personarum in divinis, de processione Spiritus a Filio, de peccato originis, & necessitate gratiae alicujus internae, ut aliquis bene operari possit, & ad salutem utiliter. Etenim ista ex Scripturis non satis clare deduci, ut citra traditionis authoritatem haberi possint pro fidei dogmatis, inde probant quod haeretici, ut hodie Graeci, & olim Ariani & Pelagiani, contra ista ex Scripturis istis probabiliter disputant, neque tantum respondent argumentis, quibus articuli illi ex Scriptura sacra confirmantur, sed vicissim ex Scripturis pro sua sententia loca non pauca cum specie objiciunt. Itaque nunquam posse controversias cum hominibus protervis finiri, nisi sit praeter Scripturam aliud Dei verbum quod dogmata ista clarius confirmet, & unde possit verus Scripturae sacrae sensus circa loca controversa peti certo & infallibiliter.
pass_a_gloss: But against this the adversaries urge, that there are not a few things which are of great moment for faith, which are indeed deduced from Scripture in some way; But not so certainly and evidently that the mind can firmly rest in it, and all doubt be removed, until the authority of tradition be applied, which confirms the true sense of sacred Scripture, and puts it beyond doubt. And for example they bring the doctrine of the equality of the persons in the Godhead, of the procession of the Spirit from the Son, of original sin, and of the necessity of some internal grace, that someone may be able to work well, and usefully unto salvation. For that these are not deduced from the Scriptures clearly enough to be held as dogmas of faith apart from the authority of tradition, they prove thence that heretics, as today the Greeks, and formerly the Arians and Pelagians, dispute against these from those Scriptures with probability, and not only answer the arguments by which those articles are confirmed from sacred Scripture, but in turn object from the Scriptures not a few places with a show for their own opinion. Therefore controversies with stubborn men can never be finished, unless besides Scripture there be another word of God which confirms those dogmas more clearly, and whence the true sense of sacred Scripture about the controversial places can be sought certainly and infallibly.
pass_b_english: Rome lists weighty doctrines drawn from Scripture only 'somehow' — Trinity equality, Filioque, original sin, need of inward grace.
Until tradition seals the sense, they say, the mind cannot rest without doubt.
Heretics (Greeks, Arians, Pelagians) quote Scripture both ways with a show of probability.
So they demand another divine word to end controversy infallibly.
